[=''[[Nepenthes abalata|N. abalata]]/N. alata''] }} |}} '''''Nepenthes alata''''' ({{IPAc-en|n|ᵻ|ˈ|p|ɛ|n|θ|iː|z|_|ə|ˈ|l|ɑː|t|ə}}; from [[Latin]] ''alatus'' "winged") is a tropical [[pitcher plant]] [[endemism|endemic]] to the [[Philippines]]. Like all pitcher plants, it is [[carnivore|carnivorous]] and uses its nectar to attract insects that drown in the pitcher and are digested by the plant. It is highly [[polymorphism (biology)|polymorphic]], and its taxonomy continues to be subject to revisions. ==Description== [[File:Nepenthes alata unbudded flowers.jpg|alt=|left|thumb|Developing seed pods.]] ''N. alata'' can vary strongly in colouration and morphology. The [[floral formula]] is ✶ K4 A4+4+1* G0 for staminate (the apical stamen /*/ may not be present) and ✶ K4 A0 {{underline|G}}(4) for pistillate flowers.{{Cite book | publisher = Cambridge University Press | isbn = 978-0-521-49346-8 | last = Ronse De Craene | first = Louis P. | title = Floral Diagrams: An Aid to Understanding Flower Morphology and Evolution | location = Cambridge | date = 2010-02-04 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=24p-LgWPA50C | page = 165 }} ==Taxonomy== ''Nepenthes alata'' has long been treated as a highly [[Polymorphism (biology)|polymorphic]] species spanning all the major islands of the [[Geography of the Philippines|Philippine archipelago]] (with the possible exception of [[Palawan]]).McPherson, S.R. & V.B. Amoroso 2011. ''[[Field Guide to the Pitcher Plants of the Philippines]]''. Redfern Natural History Productions, Poole. Under this broad [[Circumscription (taxonomy)|circumscription]], ''N. alata'' was understood to have an altitudinal range of {{convert|0|–|1900|m|ft|abbr=on}} [[above sea level]] and was recorded from, among others, the islands of [[Bohol (island)|Bohol]], [[Camiguin]], [[Cebu (island)|Cebu]], [[Culion Island|Culion]], [[Leyte (island)|Leyte]], [[Luzon]], [[Mindanao]], [[Mindoro]], [[Negros (island)|Negros]], [[Panay]], [[Samar Island|Samar]],Suarez, W. 2011. {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130201014350/http://pitcherplants.proboards.com/index.cgi?board=nepwild&action=display&thread=9702|title=Samar's ''Nepenthes alata''}}. Carnivorous Plants in the tropics, January 12, 2011.Robinson, A. 2012. [http://pitcherplants.proboards.com/index.cgi?board=nepwild&action=display&thread=11301 ''Nepenthes merrilliana'' on Samar] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120722155445/http://pitcherplants.proboards.com/index.cgi?board=nepwild&action=display&thread=11301 |date=2012-07-22 }}. Carnivorous Plants in the tropics, June 29, 2012. and [[Sibuyan Island|Sibuyan]]. ''Nepenthes alata'' in this broad sense (''[[sensu lato]]'') is one of the easiest and most popular ''[[Nepenthes]]'' in [[Plant cultivation|cultivation]].Catalano, M. 2009. ''Nepenthes''. In: ''Growing Carnivores — an Italian perspective''. Prague. pp. 50–57. In 2013, ''N. alata'' was redelimited by [[Martin Cheek]] and [[Matthew Jebb]] to encompass only those populations from northern and central [[Luzon]] with conspicuously hairy pitchers (a [[taxon]] known in horticultural circles as the "hairy ''N. alata''"). Cheek and Jebb's ''N. alata'' ''[[sensu stricto]]'' has an altitudinal distribution of {{convert|550|m|ft|abbr=on}} and above. Under this interpretation, the more southerly plants previously referred to this species actually represent the newly resurrected ''[[Nepenthes graciliflora|N. graciliflora]]'' (the "typical ''N. alata''" of horticulture; found on [[Bohol (island)|Bohol]], [[Leyte (island)|Leyte]], [[Luzon]], [[Mindanao]], [[Mindoro]], [[Panay]], [[Samar Island|Samar]], and [[Sibuyan Island|Sibuyan]]) as well as the newly described ''[[Nepenthes negros|N. negros]]'' ([[Biliran Island|Biliran]] and [[Negros (island)|Negros]]) and ''[[Nepenthes ramos|N. ramos]]'' ([[Mindanao]]).{{cite journal | last1 = Cheek | first1 = M. | last2 = Jebb | first2 = M. | year = 2013 | title = ''Nepenthes ramos'' (Nepenthaceae), a new species from Mindanao, Philippines | url = | journal = Willdenowia | volume = 43 | issue = 1| pages = 107–111 | doi = 10.3372/wi.43.43112 }} ''[[Nepenthes viridis]]'' from [[Dinagat Island|Dinagat]] and [[Samar Island|Samar]] is another close relative,{{in lang|de}} Micheler, M., T. Gronemeyer, A. Wistuba, D. Marwinski, W. Suarez & V. Amoroso 2013. ''Nepenthes viridis'', eine neue ''Nepenthes''-Art von der Insel Dinagat, Philippinen. ''[[Das Taublatt]]'' '''76''': 4–21. as are ''[[Nepenthes ceciliae|N. ceciliae]]'' (Mindanao), ''[[Nepenthes copelandii|N. copelandii]]'' (Mindanao), ''[[Nepenthes extincta|N. extincta]]'' (Mindanao), ''[[Nepenthes hamiguitanensis|N. hamiguitanensis]]'' (Mindanao), ''[[Nepenthes kitanglad|N. kitanglad]]'' (Mindanao), ''[[Nepenthes kurata|N. kurata]]'' (Mindanao), ''[[Nepenthes leyte|N. leyte]]'' (Leyte), ''[[Nepenthes mindanaoensis|N. mindanaoensis]]'' (Dinagat and Mindanao), ''[[Nepenthes saranganiensis|N. saranganiensis]]'' (Mindanao), and ''[[Nepenthes ultra|N. ultra]]'' (Luzon).{{cite journal | last1 = Cheek | first1 = M. | last2 = Jebb | first2 = M. | year = 2013 | title = Recircumscription of the ''Nepenthes alata'' group (Caryophyllales: Nepenthaceae), in the Philippines, with four new species | url = | journal = European Journal of Taxonomy | issue = 69 | pages = 1–23 | doi = 10.5852/ejt.2013.69 | doi-access = free}}{{cite journal | last1 = Cheek | first1 = M. | last2 = Jebb | first2 = M. | year = 2013 | title = ''Nepenthes ultra'' (Nepenthaceae), a new species from Luzon, Philippines | url = | journal = Blumea | volume = 58| issue = 3| pages = 241–244| doi = 10.3767/000651913X675124 | doi-access = free}}Mey, F.S. 2013. [http://carnivorousockhom.blogspot.co.uk/2013/08/the-nepenthes-alata-group-resurrection.html The ''Nepenthes alata'' group: resurrection of ''N. graciliflora'' ; ''N. ramos'' and ''N. negros'' described as new species.] ''Strange Fruits: A Garden's Chronicle'', August 27, 2013. Together these species form the so-called "''N. alata'' group", being united by a number of morphological characters including winged [[petiole (botany)|petioles]], [[Operculum (botany)|lids]] with basal ridges on the lower surface (often elaborated into appendages), and upper pitchers that are usually broadest near the base. ''Nepenthes alata'' is closely related to several other species, including ''[[Nepenthes copelandii|N. copelandii]]'', ''[[Nepenthes mindanaoensis|N. mindanaoensis]]'', and ''[[Nepenthes saranganiensis|N. saranganiensis]]''. ''[[Nepenthes eustachya]]'' from Sumatra was once considered to fall within the variability of ''N. alata'', but this was based on a misinterpretation of [[type specimen]]s; these two species do not seem closely related to each other.{{Citation needed|date=March 2009}} {| class="wikitable" text-align: left;" |+ Morphological differences between ''N. alata'' and ''N. eustachya'' (Jebb & Cheek, 1997) !
